en: A vampire hunter?
No, that's not it.
note: Player's thought after Stanley says he senses 'something more than human' (msg 18155). Follows three pause dots: '...No, that's not it.'

en: Either way,
I can't let him find out what I really am
As if you lived in the world of night...
Hahaha, forgive me. My bad habit again.
Ah, so you've come.
I was just hoping to have a word with you.
You've been on my mind, you see.
I am Stanley.
I am the curator of this museum.
Do you remember me?
My work itself is rather staid, but personally,
note: Same as #574 (slice 007); #575 'I love folklore, legends and the mysterious.' follows on the next line.

en: Welcome! How good of you to come.
But what a mysterious person you are.
You have such a mystical air about you.
<What are you reading?>
note: Answer choice (no used_in); leads to msg 18569 (#588 'So glad you asked').

en: <I have no interest in reading>
note: Answer choice (no used_in); leads to msg 18600 (#594).

en: Oh, do you have the wrong house?
I'm truly glad that you've come again.
It's a joy to count you as a friend.
What do you want me to do...
I feel kind of tired...
I'm sleepy, and I feel sick.
My master...
note: Then '{NAME}, my master...' (#0) on the next line; the repeat is in the Japanese.

en: Please, give me your orders...
My hands and legs are all scratched up. How'd that happen?
Good day. Is anyone at home?
Hello...?
Who are you, mister?
Nobody's here now. I'm minding the house.
I see. I came to introduce myself, but...
I'm Wayne. I'm 14.
Do you live near here? Nice to meet you, mister.
Oh, it's you, mister.
Are you all alone again?
Yep. I'm minding the house.
Papa and Mama still aren't home.
You came again, mister?
Aww, I wish I could go out and play too.
The empty lot by the factory is really fun.
They say odd stuff is buried there sometimes.
But I get scolded if I don't mind the house.
I wanna go out and play...
Oh! You're back again, mister?
It's like you're coming to see me,
and that kinda makes me happy.
What kind of work do you do, mister?
<That's a secret>
note: Answer choice (no used_in); leads to msg 21313 (#691).

en: <I'm looking for someone>
note: Answer choice (no used_in); leads to msg 21325 (#693).

en: Aww, you won't tell me...
Tell me when we're better friends, OK?
Really? Is it someone you like, mister?
I hope you find them. See you!
note: 'them': the person sought is not identified.

en: Hello,
note: Before the name: 'Hello, {NAME}.' Variants: msg 21341 'Hello, Mister ' (+ name + #696 '.'); Robin 111322/111874 and Maud 267397/268082 have #152 '...' right after, so 'Hello' without comma.
'Mister' moved into the #695 variant for msg 21341: 'Hello, Mister {NAME}.'

en: Is coming here all the time your work too?
Papa and Mama are always working too.
Hey, take me outside sometime, mister.
I can't even go to school. It's so boring.
What can I do for you? I'm the only one home.
Papa and Mama are at work. Sorry.
I think you should come back later.
Hello, mister.
Lucky you, free to walk around outside.
I'm already sick of minding the house.
Huh? You're back again?
note: Shared with Daniel 197807/198436 (next line: 'Mister, are you a detective or something?').

en: Is it something I wouldn't understand even if you told me?
Wow, come in, mister!
Stay and talk with me for once.
I won't tell Papa and Mama, I promise.
Back again?
note: Shared with Daniel 197697/198317 after 'You're quite the oddball, mister.'

en: I'm glad when you come over, mister.
'Cause minding the house alone is boring.
Hello. Is anybody home?
Hello...?
Who are you, mister?
I see. I just came by today to say hello.
. And you?
